findings.highlight: at 1 o'clock on Sunday
findings.evidenceJa: 土曜の１時
findings.explanation: Mari originally said Saturday at one, which Haruki comically interpreted as Saturday afternoon rather than the extended late-night Saturday hour. The translation changes her wording to Sunday at one and removes the ambiguity that caused his mistaken daytime objection.
findings.japanese:
最初、『土曜の１時にこの前三人で飲んだ店』と
言われた時には、『昼間だと開いてないんじゃ？』と、
思いっきり的外れな指摘をしてしまったっけ。
findings.todokanai: At first, when Mari-san initially decided for us to meet up at the bar the three of us went to before, at 1 o'clock on Sunday, I suddenly asked the off-point question of "A bar open during the day?".

findings.highlight: you went all-out last Saturday, as well?
findings.evidenceJa: 先週の土日も全出だった
findings.explanation: Haruki says Mari worked full days on both Saturday and Sunday the previous weekend. The translation reduces both weekend shifts to an undefined all-out effort on Saturday alone.
findings.japanese: 「確か、先週の土日も全出だったんですよね？」
findings.todokanai: "Right, I believe you went all-out last Saturday, as well?"

findings.highlight: You joined us, so working for us is itself your job hunt.
findings.evidenceJa: ウチに入るんだからウチで働くことこそが就職活動だ
findings.explanation: Mari treats Haruki's future entry into the company as a foregone conclusion and argues that his current work there is therefore his job hunt. The translation says he has already joined the company, collapsing the distinction between part-time work and future formal employment.
findings.japanese:
「ウチに入るんだからウチで働くことこそが就職活動だ。
あんまりウダウダ言ってると内定出ても取り消すぞ」
findings.todokanai: "You joined us, so working for us is itself your job hunt. If you keep blabbering on too much, I'll revoke your job offer even if you get one."

findings.highlight: I brought up my intention of resigning and ended up displeasing Mari-san to such an extent, and as paradoxical as it is, I'm admittedly a little embarrassed.
findings.evidenceJa:
俺が辞めるって言い出すことが、
麻理さんをそこまで不機嫌にするって事実が、
逆説的ながら、少しだけ面映ゆいから。
findings.explanation: Haruki feels bashfully pleased that his resignation upsets Mari, while the translation gives only embarrassment.
findings.japanese:
俺が辞めるって言い出すことが、
麻理さんをそこまで不機嫌にするって事実が、
逆説的ながら、少しだけ面映ゆいから。
findings.todokanai: I brought up my intention of resigning and ended up displeasing Mari-san to such an extent, and as paradoxical as it is, I'm admittedly a little embarrassed.

findings.highlight: it means nothing to me for you to be satisfied
findings.evidenceJa: 何もなかったと何度言わせれば気が済むんだ
findings.explanation: Mari asks how many times she must say that nothing happened before Haruki is satisfied. The translation instead says the event means nothing to her for him to be satisfied, scrambling both her minimizing claim and the idiom about repeated reassurance.
findings.japanese: 「…何もなかったと何度言わせれば気が済むんだ？」
findings.todokanai: "How many times do I have to tell you that it means nothing to me for you to be satisfied?"

findings.highlight: Not if you didn't put it in.
findings.evidenceJa: そこは突っ込んでもらわないと
findings.explanation: Mari says Haruki was supposed to play the straight man and call out her deliberately disproportionate tissue-and-dry-cleaning joke. The translation invents a statement about nonpenetration, replacing the comic conversational request with a sexual fact claim.
findings.japanese: 「…そこは突っ込んでもらわないと」
findings.todokanai: "…Not if you didn't put it in."

findings.highlight: She's doing her very best to act cheerful around me, though there's one thing deep down in my heart that I can't ever forgive.
findings.evidenceJa: 努めて明るく振舞ってた態度を思い切りしぼませつつ、でも俺は、心の中で一つだけ承伏していなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki's own deliberately bright demeanor collapses, while inwardly he withholds assent from one part of Mari's explanation. The translation assigns the cheerful act to Mari and turns nonassent into something Haruki can never forgive.
findings.japanese:
努めて明るく振舞ってた態度を思い切りしぼませつつ、
でも俺は、心の中で一つだけ承伏していなかった。
findings.todokanai: She's doing her very best to act cheerful around me, though there's one thing deep down in my heart that I can't ever forgive.

findings.highlight: Please keep this a secret for now.
findings.evidenceJa: 今は、そうっとしておいてください
findings.explanation: Haruki asks Mari to leave him alone for the present while he cools his feelings and prepares to return. The translation asks her to keep something secret, inventing a confidentiality request instead of temporary distance.
findings.japanese:
「今は、そうっとしておいてください。
その代わり一年後、もっと使える奴になってから…
胸を張って、麻理さんの下に戻ってきますから」
findings.todokanai: "Please keep this a secret for now. In exchange for that, I'll become a more useful guy in a year… And then I'll puff out my chest and come back to work under you."

findings.highlight: "This isn't work, but a private matter. Isn't it okay to be just a little irresponsible?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「これは仕事じゃなくてプライベートなんですから。
少しは甘えがあったっていいじゃないですか」
findings.explanation: Haruki says some dependence or self-indulgence is acceptable in private life, but the translation says some irresponsibility is acceptable.
findings.japanese:
「これは仕事じゃなくてプライベートなんですから。
少しは甘えがあったっていいじゃないですか」
findings.todokanai: "This isn't work, but a private matter. Isn't it okay to be just a little irresponsible?"

findings.highlight: she's only wearing her shirt
findings.evidenceJa: シャツははだけ、ベルトも外し、スカートのホックさえも
findings.explanation: Mari has loosened or opened her shirt, removed her belt, and even undone her skirt hook. The translation says she is wearing only her shirt, falsely removing the skirt and making her substantially more undressed than the source describes.
findings.japanese:
いつの間にか、シャツははだけ、
ベルトも外し、スカートのホックさえも…
findings.todokanai: Before I noticed it, she's only wearing her shirt. She's unfastened her belt and even the hook on her skirt…

findings.highlight: I can only deduce that she was confessing something ridiculous to me from the way she seemed deep in thought and how her complexion flared up instantly…
findings.evidenceJa:
ただ、麻理さんのその思い詰めた表情と、
一気に燃え上がっていった顔色から、
今、とてつもない告白をしでかしたってことだけ…
findings.explanation: Haruki recognizes that Mari has made a momentous confession, but the translation calls it ridiculous.
findings.japanese:
ただ、麻理さんのその思い詰めた表情と、
一気に燃え上がっていった顔色から、
今、とてつもない告白をしでかしたってことだけ…
findings.todokanai: I can only deduce that she was confessing something ridiculous to me from the way she seemed deep in thought and how her complexion flared up instantly…

findings.highlight: a superior who's spoiled by her subordinates
findings.evidenceJa: ここまで部下に甘い上司
findings.explanation: Haruki says he has never known a boss this indulgent toward a subordinate. The translation reverses the direction and calls Mari a boss who is spoiled by her subordinates.
findings.japanese:
俺は、ここまで部下に甘い上司を知らない。
多分、これから一生そんな上司に出会うこともない。
findings.todokanai: I don't know a superior who's spoiled by her subordinates. And I can't imagine myself meeting a superior like her ever again in my whole life.

findings.highlight: "U-Umm… Why are you going out of your way to ask me a question like that? Aren't you someone who goes straight to violating others without a word?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「え、ええと…何でそんなことわざわざ聞くんだ？
何も言わずに犯そうとした奴が」
findings.explanation: Mari refers to Haruki as someone who tried to violate her without asking, but the translation makes the description habitual and plural.
findings.japanese:
「え、ええと…何でそんなことわざわざ聞くんだ？
何も言わずに犯そうとした奴が」
findings.todokanai: "U-Umm… Why are you going out of your way to ask me a question like that? Aren't you someone who goes straight to violating others without a word?"

findings.highlight: I don't want you to hate me anymore, Mari-san.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺、もう、麻理さんの嫌がることはしないから
findings.explanation: Haruki promises that he will no longer do anything Mari dislikes. The translation turns that conduct-based consent commitment into a wish that Mari not hate him, shifting the priority from her boundaries to his desired emotional outcome.
findings.japanese:
「…あの時はごめんなさい。
俺、もう、麻理さんの嫌がることはしないから」
findings.todokanai: "…I'm really sorry for what happened back then. It's just that I don't want you to hate me anymore, Mari-san."

findings.highlight: this is different from the horrible way things transpired back then
findings.evidenceJa: あの時の劣情とは違う
findings.explanation: Haruki distinguishes his present feeling from the base lust that drove him before. The translation compares the present with how events transpired, erasing that his point is a change in motive rather than simply a different sequence of acts.
findings.japanese: だって、あの時の劣情とは違う。
findings.todokanai: After all, this is different from the horrible way things transpired back then.

findings.highlight: I'll do my best to not let that happen.
findings.evidenceJa: 直前で拒まれても、必死で止まってみせる
findings.explanation: Haruki says that even if Mari rejects him at the last instant, he will make himself stop. After describing the rejection, 'not let that happen' reads as preventing the rejection or stop, reversing the explicit commitment to halt.
findings.japanese:
だから、直前で拒まれても、
必死で止まってみせる。
findings.todokanai: That's why even if she rejects me before I can do that, I'll do my best to not let that happen.

findings.highlight: this is something we should really discuss later on
findings.evidenceJa: それは本当に後日談でしかなくて
findings.explanation: Mari says the eventual half-year separation and breakup were merely the epilogue; the damaging cycle had begun much earlier. The translation postpones the topic for later discussion, destroying the chronology that introduces her actual explanation.
findings.japanese: 「とは言っても、それは本当に後日談でしかなくて」
findings.todokanai: "Even so, this is something we should really discuss later on."

findings.highlight: those who should enjoy their work but don't
findings.evidenceJa: 楽しめるくせに楽しまない奴
findings.explanation: After condemning escape into work, Mari says she cannot stand people who are capable of enjoying life or themselves but refuse to do so. The translation makes work the object of enjoyment, undercutting the contrast between work as escape and neglected private life.
findings.japanese:
「私は、仕事に逃げる奴が許せない。
楽しめるくせに楽しまない奴が我慢できない」
findings.todokanai: "I can't forgive those who run away by immersing themselves in work. I also can't stand those who should enjoy their work but don't."

findings.highlight: when we have our lunch break
findings.evidenceJa: 午後から仕事休んで二人で役所に行って
findings.explanation: Mari's example assumes the couple takes the afternoon off work to go to city hall. The translation restricts the errand to a lunch break, changing the planned work absence in her work-versus-private-life test.
findings.japanese:
「…例えばさ、
午後から仕事休んで二人で役所に行って、
婚姻届を出そうって約束したとするよな？」
findings.todokanai: "…For example, would we promise to submit our marriage registration at the city hall when we have our lunch break?"

findings.highlight: a special report just twelve hours ago
findings.evidenceJa: １２時直前に特ダネの連絡が入って
findings.explanation: Mari asks what Haruki would do if a scoop arrived just before noon, immediately before the planned afternoon marriage-registration errand. The translation changes that clock time into twelve hours ago and breaks the collision between the two commitments.
findings.japanese:
「そ、そ、それで、本題はこっちだ。
…１２時直前に特ダネの連絡が入って、
どうしても現場に飛ぶ必要があったらお前はどうする？」
findings.todokanai: "W-W-Well, let's get to the main topic. …What would you do if you were assigned a special report just twelve hours ago and had to fly to the scene no matter what?"

findings.highlight: someone who just can't understand how to work
findings.evidenceJa: 仕事に理解のない相手とは、もう恋愛できない
findings.explanation: Mari says she can no longer date a partner who does not understand or accept her work. The translation instead rejects someone who does not understand how to work, changing compatibility with her career into the partner's general work competence.
findings.japanese:
「…ま、それ以前にそういうことしっかり
話し合っておくのが大事だけどな。
仕事に理解のない相手とは、もう恋愛できないよ、私は」
findings.todokanai: "…Well, this is something we need to discuss beforehand. I can't be in a relationship with someone who just can't understand how to work."

findings.highlight: you're the man I've been looking for
findings.evidenceJa: 私が見込んだ通りの男
findings.explanation: Mari calls Haruki a man just as promising or capable as she judged him to be, then retreats to 'junior.' The translation calls him the man she has been looking for, inflating professional confidence into a romantic search fulfilled.
findings.japanese:
「やっぱりお前は、私が見込んだ通りの男…
いや、後輩だよ」
findings.todokanai: "As I thought, you're the man I've been looking for… Well, I should say underling."

findings.highlight: everything about my world, including myself, has been a lie
findings.evidenceJa: 自分を含めた世界全部に嘘をついてます
findings.explanation: Haruki says he is actively lying to the whole world, including himself, about why he sought Mari. The translation instead says his world itself has been a lie, removing his agency and present confession of deception.
findings.japanese: 俺は今、自分を含めた世界全部に嘘をついてます。
findings.todokanai: With the way I am now, everything about my world, including myself, has been a lie.

findings.highlight: I'm only fooling myself that they're hurting so much.
findings.evidenceJa: とても痛いのに、傷を消してしまうのが怖いから、ただ、痛みだけを誤魔化したかった
findings.explanation: Haruki says the wound truly hurts, but because he fears erasing it he only wanted to mask or numb the pain. The translation says he is fooling himself that the wounds hurt, denying the real pain that makes Mari an anesthetic rather than a cure.
findings.japanese:
とても痛いのに、傷を消してしまうのが怖いから、
ただ、痛みだけを誤魔化したかったんです。
findings.todokanai: After all, I'm scared of losing these wounds despite how painful they are, and I'm only fooling myself that they're hurting so much.
